sentences.en: This is the 99% Invisible Breakdown of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《百分之九十九隐形》的宪法深度解析节目。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: And I'm Elizabeth Jo.
sentences.zh: 我是伊丽莎白·乔。

sentences.en: Today, we're discussing Article 3, which establishes the judicial branch of the federal government.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要讨论的是第三条，它确立了联邦政府的司法分支。

sentences.en: Article 3 is much shorter than the first two articles that we've covered so far.
sentences.zh: 第三条比我们前面讨论的前两条要短得多。

sentences.en: It begins,
sentences.zh: 它开头写道：

sentences.en: The judicial power of the United States shall be vested in one Supreme Court
sentences.zh: 合众국의司法权属于最高法院

sentences.en: and in such inferior courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish.
sentences.zh: 以及国会可能随时下令设立的下级法院。

sentences.en: The judges, both of the supreme and inferior courts, shall hold their offices during good behavior and shall, at stated times,
sentences.zh: 最高法院和下级法院的法官，如行为端正，得任职，并应在规定时间内

sentences.en: receive for their services a compensation which shall not be diminished during their continuance in office.
sentences.zh: 领取报酬，其在任职期间报酬不得减少。

sentences.en: Article 3 goes on to talk about the jurisdiction of the federal courts or which types of cases they're allowed to hear.
sentences.zh: 第三条接着讨论了联邦法院的司法管辖权，即他们被允许审理哪些类型的案件。

sentences.en: These include disputes about treaties, federal laws, and, of course, the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 其中包括关于条约、联邦法律以及当然还有宪法的争议。

sentences.en: But just as important as what's in Article 3 is what is not in Article 3.
sentences.zh: 但与第三条内容同等重要的是，第三条没有写什么。

sentences.en: More on that later.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们将详细探讨这一点。

sentences.en: Our guest for this episode is Adam Liptak, who covers the Supreme Court and other legal issues for The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我们这期的嘉宾是亚当·利普塔克，他为《纽约时报》报道最高法院和其他法律问题。

sentences.en: He started his career as a lawyer before transitioning to reporting almost 25 years ago.
sentences.zh: 他职业生涯开始时是一名律师，近25年前转行做记者。

sentences.en: Adam's depth of knowledge about the Supreme Court and Article 3 makes him the perfect gueSt.
sentences.zh: 亚当对最高法院和第三条的深厚知识使他成为绝佳的嘉宾。

sentences.en: we talk about the legacy of the Roberts Court, why reforming the court is so difficult,
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了罗伯茨法院的遗产、为什么改革法院如此困难，

sentences.en: and what it's like to be a Supreme Court reporter.
sentences.zh: 以及做最高法院记者是什么体验。

sentences.en: But we start with what Adam believes surprises people most about this part of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 但我们从亚当认为最让人对宪法这部分感到惊讶的地方开始。

sentences.en: I guess they think that it's an elaborate description of our sprawling federal judicial
sentences.zh: 我想他们以为这里会详细描述我们庞大的联邦司法

sentences.en: system, when in fact, all it does is create a Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 系统，而实际上，它所做的只是创建了一个最高法院。

sentences.en: It doesn't even specify its size.
sentences.zh: 它甚至没有具体说明其规模。

sentences.en: And it leaves to Congress a lot of the detail work.
sentences.zh: 它把很多细节工作留给了国会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so what are some of the important things that we should know about this part of the Constitution?
sentences.zh: 那么关于宪法的这部分，我们应该知道哪些重要的事情呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think a key point is that it's Article 3, which is to say that the framers envisioned Congress as taking the lead role.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为一个关键点是它是第三条，也就是说制定者设想国会扮演主导角色。

sentences.en: It's a little hard for us these days to imagine that, you know, a muscular legislature was supposed to be the primary actor in the constitutional structure, the lead actor.
sentences.zh: 现在我们很难想象，你知道的，一个强有力的立法机构本应是宪法结构中的主要执行者，主角。

sentences.en: Article two, you know, an energetic president executing the laws that Congress enacted.
sentences.zh: 第二条，你知道的，是一个充满活力的总统去执行国会通过的法律。

sentences.en: And then bringing up the rear, what some of the framers called the least dangerous branch.
sentences.zh: 然后殿后的是一些制定者称之为最不危险的分支。

sentences.en: its role kind of uncertain not not a very appealing job at first people didn't particularly
sentences.zh: 它的角色有点不确定，一开始并不是一个很有吸引力的工作，人们并不是特别

sentences.en: want to be supreme court justices you know the the supreme court which we'll talk about this
sentences.zh: 想成为最高法院的大法官，你知道的，最高法院，我们稍后会讨论这个，

sentences.en: over time has taken on great stature and power but in the beginning was almost an afterthought
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移获得了巨大的威望和权力，但在最初它几乎是个事后诸葛亮，

sentences.en: as a way to you know adjudicate a small set of disputes between say citizens of different states
sentences.zh: 作为一种你知道的裁决一小部分争议的方式，比如不同州公民之间的争议

sentences.en: Well, maybe that's something we could talk a bit more about.
sentences.zh: 也许这是我们可以多聊聊的一个话题。

sentences.en: You mentioned Congress having a role.
sentences.zh: 你提到了国会扮演的角色。

sentences.en: So maybe people don't quite understand what that at least theoretical power is.
sentences.zh: 所以也许人们不太理解那个至少是理论上的权力是什么。

sentences.en: So how much power does Congress have over the Supreme Court?
sentences.zh: 那么国会对最高法院有多大权力？

sentences.en: Well, for instance, it can set the size of the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 嗯，比如它可以设定最高法院的规模。

sentences.en: That's by legislation.
sentences.zh: 那是通过立法实现的。

sentences.en: You don't need a constitutional amendment.
sentences.zh: 你不需要宪法修正案。

sentences.en: It has been as small as five, as large as 10.
sentences.zh: 它曾经小到5人，大到10人。

sentences.en: And some of that court packing, call it, and court shrinking has been done for political reasons.
sentences.zh: 其中一些所谓的法院扩编和法院缩编是出于政治原因完成的。

sentences.en: Now, it's been steady at nine for a long time, and that norm may stick,
sentences.zh: 现在，它长期保持在9人，这种规范可能会坚持下去，

sentences.en: although there was a lot of talk in the Biden years from the left that the court should be expanded because of progressives' unhappiness with some of the Supreme Court's decisions.
sentences.zh: 尽管在拜登执政期间，左翼有很多言论认为应该扩大法院规模，因为进步派对最高法院的一些决定感到不满。

sentences.en: But that's one respect in which Congress has a lot of power.
sentences.zh: 但这是国会拥有很大权力的一个方面。

sentences.en: It has some power.
sentences.zh: 它确实有一些权力。

sentences.en: It's sort of untested in telling the court what cases it can hear.
sentences.zh: 它在告诉法院可以审理哪些案件方面有点未经测试。

sentences.en: And jurisdiction stripping is a thing.
sentences.zh: 而且剥夺管辖权是真实存在的。

sentences.en: For instance, in the realm of habeas corpus law, it is told the court and lower courts what
sentences.zh: 例如，在人身保护令法律领域，它告诉法院和下级法院

sentences.en: kinds of cases can be brought in federal court and what cannot.
sentences.zh: 哪些类型的案件可以在联邦法院提起，哪些不能。

sentences.en: Maybe we could pause for a moment and sort of expand that for folks who might not be
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以暂停一会儿，为那些可能不熟悉这个概念的人

sentences.en: familiar with this idea.
sentences.zh: 展开讲讲。

sentences.en: What is jurisdiction stripping exactly?
sentences.zh: 究竟什么是剥夺管辖权？

sentences.en: Well, for starters, the Supreme Court doesn't get to decide every case in the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，最高法院并不能裁决世上所有的案件。

sentences.en: It only gets to decide cases arising from federal law or the Constitution, with, you know, some scattered exceptions.
sentences.zh: 除了零星的一些例外，它只能裁决因联邦法律或宪法引起的案件。

sentences.en: But it's not a court of general jurisdiction.
sentences.zh: 但它不是一个具有一般管辖权的法院。

sentences.en: And then Congress can also tell it that it can decide some sorts of cases and not others.
sentences.zh: 然后国会还可以告诉它，它可以裁决某些类型的案件，而不能裁决其他案件。

sentences.en: And so how far Congress can go down that road is quite untested.
sentences.zh: 因此，国会在这条路上能走多远很大程度上是未经检验的。

sentences.en: but it can go down that road at least some part of the way.
sentences.zh: 但它至少可以顺着这条路走上一段。

sentences.en: So, you know, we talk about the separation of powers,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们谈到三权分立，

sentences.en: but the three branches also have intersecting powers.
sentences.zh: 但这三个分支也拥有交织的权力。

sentences.en: And Congress's power in shaping the Supreme Court
sentences.zh: 国会在塑造最高法院

sentences.en: and the federal court system is pretty substantial.
sentences.zh: 和联邦法院系统方面的权力是相当巨大的。

sentences.en: So I know that over the years,
sentences.zh: 所以我知道多年来，

sentences.en: members of Congress have proposed things like
sentences.zh: 国会议员们曾提出过这样的建议，比如

sentences.en: we want to make sure that the federal courts
sentences.zh: 我们希望确保联邦法院

sentences.en: maybe can hear issues on school desegregation
sentences.zh: 也许能够审理关于学校废除种族隔离

sentences.en: or abortion or school prayer.
sentences.zh: 或堕胎或学校祈祷的问题。

sentences.en: So these come up, I think, for political reasons, but they never get very far.
sentences.zh: 所以这些出于政治原因被提出来，但它们从未走得很远。

sentences.en: And I've always been curious why Congress has never gone maybe as far as it possibly could and test those limits.
sentences.zh: 我一直很好奇为什么国会从未尽可能地走得更远去测试那些界限。

sentences.en: I don't know if you have a view on that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你对此有什么看法。

sentences.en: I think it's a kind of deep American norm that it would be untoward.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种深层的美国规范，认为这样做是不合宜的。

sentences.en: It would be unseemly.
sentences.zh: 这是不体面的。

sentences.en: It would be unjust to do it.
sentences.zh: 这样做是不公正的。

sentences.en: But I'm not sure that the Constitution wouldn't allow it.
sentences.zh: 但我不确定宪法是否不允许这样做。

sentences.en: And I think probably if Congress were to do something along those lines, perhaps in an uncontroversial area like patent law, it ought to have to be prospective.
sentences.zh: 我想如果国会要沿着这些路线做点什么，也许在一个没有争议的领域比如专利法中，它应该是前瞻性的。

sentences.en: It would be problematic probably for Congress to say that in pending cases, the court has to do X or Y.
sentences.zh: 国会说在未决案件中法院必须做甲或乙，这可能会有问题。

sentences.en: Although there are cases that reach the court where statutes are quite specific, including by docket number, saying that they have to be resolved one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 尽管有些案件到达法院时法规相当具体，包括案号，规定必须以某种方式解决。

sentences.en: And the court has basically gone along with those congressional enactments.
sentences.zh: 而法院基本上顺从了国会的这些立法。

sentences.en: So your larger point, Elizabeth, is quite right, that we don't know how much power Congress has, but Congress hasn't tried to exercise it very much.
sentences.zh: 所以伊丽莎白，你的宏观观点是完全正确的，我们不知道国会有多少权力，但国会并没有真正去行使它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I think maybe some of the most significant cases about jurisdiction stripping and even taking some cases away, even from the Supreme Court itself, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为关于剥夺管辖权甚至剥夺某些案件（甚至从最高法院本身剥夺）的一些最重要的案件，你知道的，

sentences.en: the biggest ones go all the way back to the Civil War era.
sentences.zh: 最大的那些一直可以追溯到内战时期。

sentences.en: And that suggests that there's some, as you've mentioned, this timidity or kind of uncertainty in the Congress being reluctant to force that issue as far as it can go.
sentences.zh: 这表明正如你所提到的，国会存在某种胆怯或某种不确定性，不愿意将这个问题推向极致。

sentences.en: And maybe you're suggesting that if Congress were to go that far, maybe that would really be a pointer of – that would really point us to some sort of constitutional crisis moment.
sentences.zh: 也许你是说如果国会真的走到那一步，那可能真的是一个指标——那真的会把我们指向某种宪法危机时刻。

sentences.en: Oh, if we haven't reached that already.
sentences.zh: 哦，如果我们还没走到那一步的话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, also, the political branches are accountable to the electorate, and it's entirely possible that people wouldn't put up with it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有，政治分支对选民负责，完全有可能人们不会容忍这一点。

sentences.en: Just as FDR, who could not have been more popular in the polls and commanded super majorities of support in both houses,
sentences.zh: 正如富兰克林·罗斯福在民意调查中不可能更受欢迎，并在两院拥有压倒性多数的支持，

sentences.en: couldn't get court backing done because the public wouldn't put up with it.
sentences.zh: 却无法完成法院扩编，因为公众不会容忍。

sentences.en: And so, I mean, one reason politicians may not do it is because it's at least possible the public won't stand for it.
sentences.zh: 所以我的意思是，政客们不做这件事的一个原因是因为公众至少有可能不会买账。

sentences.en: But also, like, the Congress wouldn't stand for it.
sentences.zh: 但同时，比如国会也不会买账。

sentences.en: Like, it wasn't, like, all lockstep behind the executive back then.
sentences.zh: 就像当时它并非完全步调一致地跟在行政部门后面一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, we do live in different times.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们确实生活在不同的时代。

sentences.en: And that's also, we talked about the authority of Congress to maybe limit the kinds of cases that the federal courts and even the Supreme Court itself can hear.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们讨论过的内容，关于国会有权限制联邦法院甚至最高法院本身可以审理的案件类型。

sentences.en: But, you know, we should also mention here, Congress has a great deal of power over the very structure and funding of the courts.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们在这里也应该提到，国会对法院的结构和资金拥有巨大权力。

sentences.en: And I guess that, too, could be a kind of source of power or control from Congress.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是国会权力或控制的一种来源。

sentences.en: But we haven't seen too much of that either.
sentences.zh: 但我们也没有看到太多这种情况。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: This came up a little bit, and it's basically political statements.
sentences.zh: 这被稍微提及过，基本上是政治声明。

sentences.en: But the question of whether you can impeach judges and justices because you don't like their rulings was kind of tested early in the life of the republic.
sentences.zh: 但因为不喜欢法官的裁决而弹劾法官和大法的可行性问题，在共和国建立初期曾受到过考验。

sentences.en: And the consensus view after Samuel Chase was impeached by the House but acquitted by the Senate was that we're not going to have that kind of system,
sentences.zh: 塞缪尔·蔡斯被众议院弹劾但在参议院被宣告无罪后，大家的共识是，我们不会实行那种系统，

sentences.en: which in much of the world happens.
sentences.zh: 这在世界上很多地方都会发生。

sentences.en: You sort of get new judges with a new administration.
sentences.zh: 随着新政府上台，你会得到新法官。

sentences.en: And we will impeach judges for authentic misconduct, but not for disagreement with how they've ruled, or at least not so far.
sentences.zh: 我们将为真正的违纪行为弹劾法官，而不是因为不同意他们的裁决，至少目前为止如此。

sentences.en: So we've talked about that there isn't a lot in Article 3, but of the stuff that is in Article 3, what are some of the important things that you would teach your students,
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论过第三条内容不多，但在第三条包含的内容中，有哪些是你会教给学生的呢，

sentences.en: Elizabeth, for example, and what should we know?
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白，比如，我们应该知道什么？

sentences.en: Well, certainly some of the topics we've just discussed, this idea that Congress does have a significant role, which it hasn't always exercised to its most extreme,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然包括我们刚讨论的一些话题，即国会确实扮演了重要角色，尽管它并未总是将其发挥到极致，

sentences.en: in the kinds of cases that the federal courts in general and the Supreme Court can hear.
sentences.zh: 关于联邦法院总体以及最高法院可以审理的案件类型。

sentences.en: What's also in Article 3 is this idea that the federal courts are courts of limited jurisdiction.
sentences.zh: 第三条中还包含这样一种观点，即联邦法院是有限管辖权的法院。

sentences.en: And that's just a fancy way of saying the federal courts can't actually hear every single kind of case.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种高级说法，意指联邦法院其实不能审理每一单案件。

sentences.en: You know, your average slip and fall, your contract dispute, generally those are for the state courts.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你平常的滑倒摔伤、合同纠纷，通常是留给州法院的。

sentences.en: And in fact, most of the criminal justice cases in the country are within the state court systems rather than federal courts.
sentences.zh: 事实上，全国绝大多数刑事司法案件都在州法院系统内，而不是联邦法院。

sentences.en: So as powerful as we think the federal judiciary is, and it is, it actually can only hear a circumscribed number in different types of cases.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管我们认为联邦司法机构多么强大（它确实很强大），但它实际上只能审理数量有限、类型不同的案件。

sentences.en: So that's really important.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很重要。

sentences.en: And then I think, you know, so much of this is thinking about how the court itself has interpreted the very part of the Constitution that regulates it.
sentences.zh: 然后我认为，很多这方面的内容都在于思考法院本身是如何解释管辖宪法本身的这部分的。

sentences.en: You know, the Article 3 is just six paragraphs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，第三条只有六个段落。

sentences.en: So there's not a whole lot there.
sentences.zh: 所以并没有太多的内容。

sentences.en: I might point to a distinctive feature of the American federal judicial system, which is that judges, both of the supreme and inferior courts,
sentences.zh: 我可能会指出美国联邦司法系统的一个独特特征，即最高法院和下级法院的法官，

sentences.en: shall hold their offices during good behavior, which is to say that they have life tenure.
sentences.zh: 如行为端正，得任职，也就是说他们享有终身任期。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They can be impeached, but otherwise they get to decide when they will step down.
sentences.zh: 他们可以被弹劾，但在那之外他们自己决定何时卸任。

sentences.en: We are the only developed nation in the world without either a mandatory retirement age or term limits.
sentences.zh: 我们是世界上唯一没有强制退休年龄或任期限制的发达国家。

sentences.en: And that is not widely thought to be a good thing.
sentences.zh: 而这并不被普遍认为是一件好事。

sentences.en: It leads to questions about people serving longer than they should, about cognitive decline.
sentences.zh: 它引发了关于人们超期服役、认知衰退的问题。

sentences.en: And it also injects an element of politics at the back end of Supreme Court service.
sentences.zh: 它还在最高法院服务的后期注入了政治因素。

sentences.en: It's bad enough that Supreme Court justices are appointed through an intensely political process,
sentences.zh: 最高法院大法官是通过高度政治化的过程被任命的，这已经够糟了，

sentences.en: nominated by a politician, the president, confirmed by 100 politicians in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 由政客总统提名，由参议院的100名政客确认。

sentences.en: But then this idea of good behavior ought to give them a measure of independence,
sentences.zh: 但随后这种行为端正的理念应该赋予他们一定程度的独立性，

sentences.en: and also that their pay can't be diminished.
sentences.zh: 并且他们的薪酬不能减少。

sentences.en: So that's meant to insulate them from politics.
sentences.zh: 所以这是为了让他们免受政治干扰。

sentences.en: But then on the back end of their careers, they get to decide whom they're going to retire under.
sentences.zh: 但在他们职业生涯的后期，他们可以决定在哪个总统任下退休。

sentences.en: And they tend to try to retire under a president whose politics are simpatico with their own.
sentences.zh: 他们往往试图在政治立场与自己相符的总统任下退休。
